subject: Re: EdgeFin Performance/SLO benchmark methodology exchange
messages:
From: Priya Reddy <priya@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo and the discussion today — really helpful. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying Qs so we can scope the benchmark: 

- Latency targets: 95th pctl <= 250ms for single-turn text generation at our median prompt length (~150 tokens).
- Throughput/concurrency: our peak traffic is ~120 qps for the endpoint with sustained bursts up to 200 qps for ~10 min.
- Streaming: we need token streaming for partial results (important for our UI).
- Payloads: typical request = system + user prompt (~200-250 tokens total), sometimes with 3rd-party embeddings attached (metadata).

Can Redwood's benchmark harness measure both cold-start and warm (KV cache) behavior, and produce reproducible 95/99 latency distributions? Also happy to share a representative prompt set — attaching a v1 prompt set.

Next step: would love a proposed benchmark methodology and schedule.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Reddy
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeFin

Attachment: edgefin_benchmark_prompt_set_v1.json (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification follow-up

Hi Priya — great to connect. Appreciate the prompt set. Below is a proposed high-level benchmark methodology that we can iterate on: 

1) Objectives
- Validate Redwood dedicated config that meets 95th pctl <= 250ms at 120 qps sustained, and graceful degradation up to 200 qps.
- Verify streaming supports per-token latency <= 50ms from generation to first-byte under warm KV cache.

2) Workloads
- Use your prompt set (v1) for functional representativeness. We'll synthesize a traffic trace matching your qps/concurrency profile (peak/baseline).

3) Scenarios to run
- Cold-start (no cache, model workers scaled-down)
- Warm (KV cache primed, steady-state)
- Burst (simulate 200 qps for 10m)
- Long-tail (large prompt length distribution up to 1k tokens)

4) Metrics and measurement definitions
- Latency: measure p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (request-receive to last-byte) and first-byte for streaming.
- Throughput: sustained qps and successful requests per second.
- Concurrency: workers and KV cache hit rates.
- Reproducibility: each scenario run 3x; report mean/std and attach raw traces.

5) Harness and artifacts
- We'll run Redwood's benchmark harness (attached) that produces OpenTelemetry traces + per-request latency logs and a standard CSV output (template attached).

6) Next steps
- Confirm the target scenarios and we schedule a 2-hour run next week.

I've attached our harness (redwood_benchmark_harness_v2.zip) and a results template. Marcus will chime in on the streaming measurement approach.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_harness_v2.zip, benchmark_results_template.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya@edgefin.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification follow-up

Thanks — short note on streaming measurements:

- For streaming first-byte, we'll instrument both the server-side generation timestamp and client-side receive timestamps (we ask you to run our lightweight collector during the test).
- We define first-byte latency as time from generation token timestamp to arrival of first token frame at client; end-to-end as request start to final token received.
- We'll measure token inter-arrival jitter (median and 95th) which impacts perceived responsiveness.

One clarification: when Priya says "token streaming for partial results", is it sufficient to get a first token frame within 50ms on warm cache, or do you need progressive token frames at a specific cadence?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Reddy <priya@edgefin.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgefin.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin - Performance SLO qualification follow-up

Marcus — thanks, great questions. Our requirements: 
- First token within 50ms (warm) is critical for UX.
- We also care about steady token cadence: ideally <30ms median inter-token for short responses (~50 tokens) and <100ms p95 for longer streaming sessions.

We'll stand up the collector during the run — Tom will coordinate on our side. Happy to lock the 2-hour window on Tue 5/19.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Hi Priya — quick compliance and reproducibility notes from our side before the run tomorrow: 

- We'll produce an artifacts package with raw traces, CSV exports (see attached template), and a reproducible harness runbook that lists exact binaries, model weights/versions, quantization flags, and the Docker image SHA.
- For security needs: if you require a private VPC run, we can execute the harness in your VPC and deliver encrypted artifacts to your secure bucket.
- Please confirm whether test data can include production PII — if yes, we need a signed DPA addendum for the benchmark artifacts; otherwise please sanitize sample prompts.

Attaching the results template and the runbook checklist. Looking forward to the run — we'll share results within 48 hours of completion.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
